notes.text: Q-Chem CPU load (CPU / wall from its output, 6-31G(d)): SCF 23-30 cores; response part TDA 1.4-1.9 cores, SF-TDA 1.1, MRSF-TDA 19.3. Q-Chem 6.4 runs in parallel only through OpenMP (qchem -nt 36; MPI only for finite-difference / many-body jobs, and this install has no MPI build): the TDA and SF-TDA response is effectively serial. def2-TZVP SF-TDA: 94 % of one core (top).
Psi4 memory: MEM_DF keeps the 3-index DF tensor in core (Psi4 output 'AOs need': 5.19 GiB 6-31G(d), 26.70 GiB def2-TZVP = (1260/552)^2 x); ORCA RIJCOSX stores no 3-index K tensor.
Psi4 has no ROKS ("ROHF reference for DFT is not available"): no Psi4 ROKS row. Psi4 UKS starts from the Psi4 UKS triplet seed, which reads the RKS seed (as in ORCA and Q-Chem).

Time split, every code: SCF, s + resp, s = Wall, s of the same run. SCF = the SCF time the code reports (ORCA 'SCF iterations' module timing, Q-Chem 'SCF time ... wall', Psi4 SI-SA-REKS: wall sum of the timers before 'REKS: compute_si'); resp = the rest of the run, start-up and output included. Psi4 SI: the run time outside the Psi4 timers falls into resp.

inputs.caption: SA-REKS(6,6): threads and memory from the environment (`OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `PSI4_MEMORY`); seed orbitals read from `prev.npy` (not shipped).
SI-SA-REKS(6,6), 10 states: environment and `prev.npy` seed as for SA-REKS(6,6).
ORCA SF-TDA, 10 roots: `%pal nprocs 36` and `%maxcore 8333` (MB per rank) set in the input; seed `prev.gbw` read by `MORead` (not shipped).
Q-Chem SF-TDA, 10 roots: `mem_total 300000` (MB) set in the input, threads from `qchem -nt`; seed read by `scf_guess read` (not shipped).

definitions.time_split: SCF, s + resp, s = Wall, s: SCF = SCF time the code reports (ORCA 'SCF iterations' module, Q-Chem 'SCF time ... wall', Psi4 SI-SA-REKS: timers before 'REKS: compute_si'), resp = the rest of the run; an SCF-only job is SCF throughout
definitions.s_per_scf_iter: s / SCF it = SCF, s / SCF iterations
definitions.resp_iter: resp. it = Davidson iterations of the response (1 (direct) = SI of dimension <= 4000 solved by one dense LAPACK diagonalization)
definitions.s_per_resp_iter: s / resp. it = resp, s / resp. it
